sections.heading: What changed in the synthetic environment
sections.summary: Three fictional infrastructure signals are organized by decision relevance rather than novelty.

evidence.claim: A synthetic benchmark reports lower queue latency after deterministic batching.

implications: Batching policy can matter more than model size in constrained systems.
actions: Reproduce the benchmark before changing a production queue.

sections.heading: Why the mechanism could matter
sections.summary: The fixture separates measured latency from a causal explanation about scheduler behavior.

evidence.claim: The synthetic trace records fewer context switches under the revised scheduler.

implications: Operational gains may disappear at different request-size distributions.
actions: Test small, medium and burst workloads independently.

sections.heading: Adoption gate and counter-case
sections.summary: A fictional comparison highlights migration cost, observability requirements and rollback design.

evidence.claim: The comparison environment has complete rollback receipts for every synthetic deployment.

implications: A technically faster path can still be inferior when rollback evidence is weak.
actions: Require a reversible pilot and explicit acceptance metrics.

sections.heading: Next signals to verify
